old_statement_line: "statement": "ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Attempt the non-amenable direction through the spectral radius criterion of Benjamini-Schramm and Hutchcroft's p_c <= 1/spectral radius... type bounds. Result: Known route: if p_c < 1/rho where rho is the spectral radius of simple random walk, then at p slightly above p_c the expected number of open paths of length n to distance n grows slower than the number of returns... this gives p_c < p_u for graphs where p_c(G) < 1/(rho ... ) and is the content of the Benjamini-Schramm 1996 criterion p_c < 1/(1 + spectral gap)?; the general conjecture needs p_c < p_u even when p_c is close to 1/rho... For groups with p_c(G) < 1/rho(G) the conjecture holds; the remaining case is groups with a Cayley graph where p_c >= 1/rho, and the Pak-Smirnova trick replaces the generating set to make p_c small relative to rho. So the conjecture in its generating-set-free form (some Cayley graph) is settled by Pak-Smirnova, while the conjecture for EVERY Cayley graph reduces to showing p_c(G) < 1/rho(G)^{?}... I checked the inequality p_c <= 1/(1 + h) where h is the Cheeger constant... Benjamini-Schramm prove p_c <= 1/(1+h) and p_u >= 1/(1+h)?? no. The honest reduction: for every Cayley graph, p_c < p_u would follow from p_c < 1/rho (Benjamini-Schramm criterion) and the open question is whether every non-amenable Cayley graph satisfies p_c < 1/rho, which fails? For the free group with the standard generators p_c = 1/(2d-1) and 1/rho = (2d-1)/(2 sqrt(2d-1)) > p_c, consistent. No counterexample and no proof. Obstruction: Need p_c(G) < 1/rho(G) or another uniform criterion for every Cayley graph of every non-amenable group.",
new_statement_line: "statement": "AUDIT CORRECTION (w559, 2026-10-10; independent review pending) of the 2026-09-07 C0047-A001 spectral route. For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected d-regular simple Cayley graph G, let rho=||A_G||/d denote the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius. Benjamini-Schramm 1996, Theorem 4, printed p.76 (bond extension in section 2), and Juschenko-Nagnibeda 2015, Theorem 2, give the sufficient condition d*rho*p_c(G)<1 for p_c(G)<p_u(G). The original p_c<1/rho quotation omitted d and is not that criterion: it is automatic when rho<1 and p_c<=1. Nonamenability does not imply the repaired criterion for a prescribed generating set. In the simple Cayley graph C_2*C_3 with generators {a,b,b^-1}, p_c=q is the root of 2q^2+2q^3-2q^4=1 in (0.63,0.64), p_u=1, and ||A||>=2, so d*rho*p_c>1.26. This counterexample refutes only the stronger universal spectral bridge. An existence theorem for a favorable generating multiset does not establish the result for every prescribed simple generating set. The parent conjecture is not solved by this packet; current 2026 openness is UNKNOWN because a recent public full-result claim has not received a mathematical or comparator proof check here.",
